page: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-64 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. It features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 54 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES cryptography. The instance is configured with 976 GB of dedicated RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 15.25 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded performance. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 54,571.25 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,654.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 293.92 GB/sec, while Geekbench software compilation and ray tracing tests also demonstrated strong tier results. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 150.66 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations. Database operations on PassMark scored 26,047.32, indicating high efficiency for memory-bound transactional tasks, while Redis SET operations reached 53.57 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m3-megamem-64 is designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads where resource density is critical. The high memory capacity relative to compute resources makes it suitable for hosting large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, and complex data analytics pipelines. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which should be factored into architectural planning. This instance is best suited for large-scale database hosting, memory-bound ETL processes, and high-throughput transactional applications.
